pr_title: kubelet --node-ip flag using  unspecified IPs and external cloud provider node addresses behavior
pr_body:
/kind documentation
/kind bug

When the kubelet is using a external cloud provider and starts with the -node-ip flag set to an IP address (except 0.0.0.0 or ::), it creates the Node object with that IP and adds an annotation `alpha.kubernetes.io/provided-node-ip` to the Node  to indicate the cloud provider to use only that IP on the node.status.addresses. In theory, this filtering behavior can not be changed because it can break the node approver CSR logic https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/125300#issuecomment-2148369463 , although is debatable the CSR logic is completely correct.

Before https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121028 , the kubelet , if no --node-ip was set, started populating the node.status.addresses based on default discovery mechanism , and later the external cloud provider override them. Since the default discovery is "use the IP associated to the default gateway for IPv4", this breaks IPv6 clusters where all the hostNetwork Pods created before the cloud controller manager could update the addresses, will have IPv4 addresses.

The main problem now is to support external cloud providers that are deployed as Pods, since this present a chicken an egg problem, that the external cloud provider will need an initial valid IP to be populated. Using the node-ip flag with one IP can solve the problem but has some edges, it requires to know the IP beforehand and it filter the rest of IPs the cloud provider may want to add and other components will depend on them.

The node-ip flag already has different semantics for the unspecified addresses `0.0.0.0` or `::` to mean "discovery", as in _use the IP associated to the default gateway of the corresponding IP family_. This PR gives the same meaning to this flag when used with external cloud providers, and it allows to bootstrap the node with the IP of the desired IP family, and it allows to override it by the external cloud provider without filtering.


```release-note
The kubelet, when using --cloud-provider=external can use the --node-ip flag with one of the unspecified addresses 0.0.0.0 or ::, to create the Node with the IP of the default gateway of the corresponding IP family and then delegating the responsibility to the external cloud provider. This solve the bootstrap problems of out of tree cloud providers that are deployed as Pods within the cluster.
```

Fixes: #125348

2. the --node-ip flag filtering is a bug IMHO, the justification about the CSR certificate problem only works if there are internalIPs, if there are other types of node.status.address it will fail.
3. revert will break the people that adapted since 1.29

I'm in favor of this because is easy to think about since it implements the same semantics we added to the --node-ip without external cloud provider and makes the perfect balance

issue_context.title: Change in `kubelet --node-ip` behavior in 1.29 breaks some deployment models on clouds
issue_context.body:
(from #125300)

#121028 changed kubelet's startup behavior when using an external cloud provider, so that it no longer tries to guess the right primary node IP before the cloud-controller-manager starts (since in the case where it guessed wrong, this would cause problems). But this means it can no longer set `pod.status.hostIP` / host-network `pod.status.podIP` on pods created before the ccm starts, which breaks some deployment models involving using static pods to bootstrap the cluster. (In particular, this is breaking some OpenShift functionality, which assumed that kubelet could deploy etcd and/or kube-apiserver via static pods and pass the node IP to them via the downward API.)

One suggested workaround for this problem is for the administrator to pass `--node-ip` to kubelet, but that suggestion runs into the problem that doing this would cause the node's `node.status.addresses` to be stripped of secondary addresses, which may have further side effects, if there is software that assumes that all node IPs will be listed in `node.status.address`. #125300 considered changing the way ccm treats `--node-ip` to make it _not_ strip secondary node IPs when `--node-ip` was used, but as pointed out there, this _also_ threatens to break other things, since some existing software may be depending on the fact that this behavior _does_ happen.

We briefly thought that the problem could be solved by passing `--node-ip 0.0.0.0`, but it turns out that this doesn't actually do anything different from just not passing `--node-ip`.

/sig network
/sig node
comments: It's not about the cloud provider behavior, it's about kubelet's behavior. The problem is that if you start kubelet with `--cloud-provider external` and either no `--node-ip` or `--node-ip 0.0.0.0` or `--node-ip ::`, then kubelet will not fill in `node.status.addresses`.

> that suggestion runs into the problem that doing this would cause the node's `node.status.addresses` to be stripped of secondary addresses, which may have further side effects, if there is software that assumes that all node IPs will be listed in `node.status.address`

External providers have to update node status addresses dynamically with the full set of addresses. The kubelet reacts dynamically to that and gets an updated serving certificate, so that should all work dynamically and correctly.

> External providers have to update node status addresses dynamically with the full set of addresses.

They only do that if you _don't_ pass `--node-ip` to kubelet. If you pass `--node-ip` to kubelet to override the default choice of node IP, then the cloud provider will omit all other InternalIPs from `node.status.addresses`. (This was ~always the case for legacy cloud providers and has been the case for external cloud providers at least since "before they were cool".)

> They only do that if you don't pass --node-ip to kubelet.

Well, that seems like the spot to change if you want external providers report more addresses.

Reverting kubelet to report auto-detected-and-known-to-sometimes-be-incorrect addresses when running in external cloud provider mode seems like the wrong way to fix this.

review_comments: the commit message still says "document kubelet node-ip with cloud provider external", but should be updated to clarify that it's actually changing it
